latest_release.body:
# Switchyard v0.3.0

Switchyard 0.3.0 adds reusable runner integrations, Advisor Gate and Composite routing, Auto presets, and updated Rust and Python embedding APIs. It also fixes provider translation and tool-loop behavior and removes the legacy Python server and coding-agent launchers.

This is a breaking upgrade for library and Python CLI users. Review the migration notes below before upgrading.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Switchyard/blob/v0.3.0/CHANGELOG.md#030) · [Changes since v0.2.0](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Switchyard/compare/v0.2.0...v0.3.0)

## Routing and integrations

- Advisor Gate lets an executor model work with a stronger advisor for review, approval, and redo decisions, with session review budgets and stall checkpoints.
- Composite routing combines an LLM classifier with Stage Router. Auto presets provide capable and efficient Stage configurations.
- The new `switchyard-runner` crate loads TOML deployments and runs routing in-process. NeMo Relay and LiteLLM integrations use the native routing path.
- Sub-agent routing, per-target system prompts and reasoning effort, and per-client request deadlines provide more control over agent traffic.
- DeepSWE v1.1 and NeMo Gym/LiteLLM examples document reproducible evaluation setups. Their results apply to the documented configurations, not every deployment.

## Library and Python APIs

- Python requires 3.10 or newer; the core package has no runtime dependencies.
- Python streaming exposes `Step.CallModel` and `Step.Done`, with response dictionaries and async iterators.
- Routing outcomes report ordered `selected_model_ids`, bounded decision metadata, and evidence through Rust, Python, logs, and OpenTelemetry.
- The decision endpoint supports routing without executing the selected answer model.

## Compatibility and correctness

- Provider translation preserves tool allowlists, parallel-call limits, native tool history, reasoning signatures, citations, and terminal Responses output. Unsupported cross-format native output fails explicitly.
- Streaming fixes retain late response IDs, fragmented tool names, empty tool inputs, and tool-use stop reasons.
- Responses continuations return to the provider that holds their state. Cross-format continuations retain conversation history in process memory; records are lost on restart.
- Media and tool-result translation preserves supported image, audio, document, and file payloads.
- Credential redaction and header handling protect request trust boundaries. Failed or abandoned streams count as errors, and usage reporting preserves translated cache-write and thinking tokens.

## Migration and removals

- The Python `switchyard` command, `switchyard serve`, coding-agent wrappers, YAML route bundles, legacy server stack, and compatibility bindings are removed. Connect clients to the standalone `switchyard-server` with native TOML configuration.
- Package extras `[server]`, `[all]`, `[cli]`, `[tracing]`, and `[affinity-redis]` are removed. The Python package declares no optional dependency extras.
- `classify_trigger` replaces `session_affinity`; use `classify_trigger = "new_session"` for the previous session-affinity behavior.
- Rust and Python embedding callers must adopt the updated step and routing-outcome APIs. Rust struct literals may also need the new `Response.upstream_headers` and `Metadata.subagent_identity_unsupported` fields.

## Install

After the tag-triggered package publishing workflow completes, install the Python bindings with:

```bash
pip install nemo-switchyard==0.3.0
```

Install the standalone server separately:

```bash
cargo install --locked switchyard-server --version 0.3.0
```

See the [getting-started guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Switchyard/blob/v0.3.0/docs/getting_started.md) for configuration and source builds.

## Limitations

The standalone server remains a demo/evaluation component. Release validation covers Ubuntu 24.04 on Linux x86_64; other platforms are outside th

detail.readme:
# NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard

Switchyard is an open-source library that helps an AI agent choose which model handles each request. It combines efficient models with more capable models so you can balance task success, cost, and latency on your workload. Adopt Switchyard by embedding its Rust core, **libsy**, in your gateway or agent harness. You own the model clients, credentials, and service. Switchyard supplies the routing decision.

Quickstart  ·  Documentation  ·  Benchmarks  ·  What’s new  ·  Roadmap  ·  Releases  ·  Contributing

## How it works 1. Configure the models an agent can use and choose a routing algorithm. 2. The algorithm examines the request or the agent's recent tool activity. Some algorithms call a model to judge the task. 3. A gateway or agent sends the request to the selected model. Routing can change as the agent continues its work. Evaluate the complete agent, model pool, and routing configuration against your single-model baseline. A cheaper model call does not guarantee a cheaper successfully completed task. The [tuning loop](docs/tuning/index.md) gives the steps for that evaluation, and [Troubleshooting](docs/operations/troubleshooting.md) lists the settings that disable routing without an error. ## How to use it - **[Through an existing gateway](#through-an-existing-gateway):** Use an available gateway integration. - **[Embed libsy in your harness](#embed-libsy-in-your-harness):** Add libsy to a service you operate. - **[Evaluate Switchyard locally](#evaluate-switchyard-locally):** Compare routing configurations with your own model pool using the demo server. ### Through an existing gateway | Gateway | Start here | Deployment and limits | | --- | --- | --- | | **Agent Router** | [Agent Router](https://github.com/tetratelabs/built-on-envoy/blob/main/extensions/switchyard/README.md) | Open-source and self-hosted. It provides an OpenAI-compatible API and runs on Envoy. | | **LiteLLM** | [Run the Switchyard routing-plugin example](examples/litellm/README.md#quick-start-with-the-local-proxy) | Experimental and checkout-only. The example pins LiteLLM 1.102.0 and supports Stage routing based on request history, plus Random routing. It cannot service intermediate model calls required by classifier or escalation algorithms. | | **NeMo Relay** | [Build and configure the native plugin](crates/switchyard-nemo-relay-plugin/README.md#build-from-source) | Requires Relay `>=0.10.0, <1.0.0`. The source-build path requires a Rust toolchain and Python 3. | | **OpenRouter** | [Use Switchyard through OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/routers/switchyard-router) | Hosted by OpenRouter. Set `model` to `nvidia/switchyard` in API requests. | Relay 0.8.x and 0.9.0 can lose upstream error status and details when the plugin is enabled, even for models outside its routes. Review the [upstream error compatibility note](docs/integrations/nemo_relay.md#upstream-error-compatibility) before enabling the plugin. LiteLLM and NeMo Relay run in your own deployment. Follow each gateway's guidance for credentials and service operation. ### Embed libsy in your harness `Algorithm::run_stream` hands model calls and the final routing outcome back to your application. In this development-API outline, comments mark the work your code supplies: ```rust let mut steps = algorithm.run_stream(request, models, state); while let Some(step) = steps.next().await { match step? { Step::CallModel(call) => { // Send call.request through your LLM client. // Give the call future to call.respond(...).await. } Step::CallDecision(call) => { // Send call.request through your decision-model client. // Give its typed response future to call.respond(...).await. } Step::Done(outcome) => { match outcome.response { Some(response) => { // Return this answer; no final LLM call is needed. } None => { // Send outcome.request through your client for the final answer, // or pass it to your gateway to make that call later. } } } } } ``` - **Inputs:** supply an algorithm, model pool, request, and state. - **Calls:** your clients handle model calls. Stage returns a selection; other algorithms may return an answer. - **Start here:** [Rust quickstart](docs/getting_started.md) · [Python bindings](docs/reference/host_integration.md#python-bindings). ### Evaluate Switchyard locally The standalone server is provided only for demos and local evaluation. It is not a supported production deployment path. [Evaluate routing locally](docs/operations/local_evaluation.md) with the standalone server and your own model pool, then [verify routing is active](docs/operations/local_evaluation.md#verify-routing-is-active). The experimental [desktop and terminal quickstart](experimental/switchyard-desktop/README.md) covers local installation, coding-tool connections, sessions, usage, recovery, and uninstall. Agent-specific guides are available for [pi](docs/integrations/pi.md) and [Oh My Pi](docs/integrations/oh_my_pi.md). ## Routing algorithms Start with Auto. Choose Task, Execution, or Composite when you need more control. These names describe routing choices. The configuration keys are unchanged. | Choice | How it chooses | TOML configuration | | --- | --- | --- | | **[Auto](docs/routing_algorithms/overview.md#auto)** | Uses the current default: Execution (Stage), efficient-first, with a confidence threshold of 0.5 and no classifier call. | `type = "auto"` | | **[Task](docs/routing_algorithms/llm_classifier_routing.md)** | A model judges whether the efficient model can handle the task. | `type = "llm_classifier"`, `mode = "capability"` | | **[Execution](docs/routing_algorithms/stage_router_routing.md)** | Uses recent tool activity and outcome signals to choose a model as the agent runs. | `type = "stage_router"` | | **[Composite](docs/routing_algorithms/composite_routing.md)** | Combines Task and Execution: a classifier sets the default model tier when execution signals are uncertain. | `type = "composite"` | Auto is a fixed preset in v0.3.0. It does not compare strategies at runtime. The TOML runner supports `type = "auto"`. In Rust, use `StageRouterConfig::new(PickerMode::EfficientFirst, 0.5)` for the same preset. The [routing overview](docs/routing_algorithms/overview.md) lists all strategies, including the [Plan/Execute configuration for Stage](docs/routing_algorithms/stage_router_routing.md#plan-and-execute), [escalation](docs/routing_algorithms/escalation_router_routing.md), [advisor](docs/routing_algorithms/advisor_gate_routing.md), [sub-agent](docs/routing_algorithms/subagent_routing.md), and [random](docs/routing_algorithms/random_routing.md). Integration support varies: check the gateway guide before choosing an algorithm. [Prefill routing](docs/routing_algorithms/prefill_routing.md) is designed for fast, efficient model selection using a model's prefill activations and a classifier trained on your own evaluation data. ## Evaluation and reference [Compare benchmark results and configs](docs/benchmarks.md) for Terminal-Bench 2.1 and DeepSWE. For latency and routing overhead testing, see [Soak Testing](docs/operations/soak_test.md). ### Further reading - [Benchmark setup and profiles](benchmark/README.md): run your own baseline and routing comparisons. - [Mechanics of Libsy](docs/mechanics_of_libsy.md): steps, model calls, and routing outcomes. - [TOML schema](docs/reference/toml_schema.md): configuration fields and defaults. - [Rust crate reference](docs/reference/rust_api.md): core and optional integration crates. - [Installation](INSTALLATION.md): package and platform requirements. ## Components Pre-1.0 software. APIs, configuration, and routing behavior can change between releases. Pin the version you integrate. | Component | Stability | Use it for | Guidance | |---|---|---|---| | `switchyard-libsy` | **Beta** | Routing embedded in your own gateway or harness. You own model calls, credentials, and retries. | Trial integrations. API will change before v1.0. | | `switchyard-llm-client` | **Alpha** | HTTP model calls and protocol translation alongside libsy. | Experiments and pilots. | | `switchyard-runner` | **Alpha** | Running configured routes inside another runtime, such as NeMo Relay. | Integration work and supervised pilots. | | `switchyard-server` | **Demo** | A standalone OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible proxy. | Demos and local evaluation only; not a supported production path. | ![Switchyard Components](docs/assets/switchyard-components.png) ## What’s new Features and integrations recently merged into `main`. - **2026-11-12 · Route Copilot Chat in VS Code**\ Pair a capable and an efficient model, and let Auto routing pick one for each request in Copilot Chat. [Setup guide →](examples/vscode/README.md) - **2026-10-16 · Route between Sonnet and Opus in Claude Code**\ Use your Claude login for automatic routing on Linux x86_64 and see the selected model in the status line. [Setup guide →](examples/claude/README.md) - **2026-10-15 · Use decision models in composite routing**\ Use Mercury Decide to judge tasks and Stage routing to adjust model selection as tools run. [Example configuration →](dev-server/config.toml) - **2026-10-13 · Use Jev to choose between models**\ Configure Jev as a task judge with candidate descriptions and a probability cutoff. [Configuration guide →](docs/routing_algorithms/composite_routing.md#decision-model-classifier) - **2026-10-12 · Bring Switchyard to TypeScript and Pi**\ Select models in Node.js or try automatic routing through Pi’s virtual models. [TypeScript bindings →](bindings/typescript/README.md) · [Pi example →](examples/pi/README.md) ## Community and license [Report an issue](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Switchyard/issues) · [Contribute](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [Code of conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) [Apache 2.0](LICENSE).
